instruction.text: Aiden has read through <mat>2/5</mat> of his book over the weekend. What is the decimal equivalent of <mat>2/5</mat>?

atoms.a: Now write the division as a decimal number.
If Aiden has read 22 Pages, how many pages are in the whole book?

hint.text: To figure out the whole, try to figure out what <mat>1/5</mat> of the book would be and then multiply by 5.

instruction.text: Ali wants to divide his Sandwich into 4 equal parts. What fraction of the sandwich will each part be, and what is the decimal equivalent?

atoms.a: If <mat>1/4</mat> of the sandwich is 55 calories, how many calories are in the whole sandwich?

instruction.text: Jamila wants to share £1 equally with her brother. What fraction of the money does each sibling get?

atoms.a: Jamila can buy 9 stickers with her 50 pence. How many stickers could she have bought with £1?

instruction.text: Dan wants to share a pizza equally between himself and his 7 friends. What fraction of the pizza does each person get?

atoms.a: After the pizza is cut into 8 slices, there are 3 pieces of tomato on each slice. How many pieces of tomato are on the whole pizza?
atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>24</gap></mat> pieces of tomato on the pizza.

instruction.text: Olivia has 3/4 of a litre of orange juice left. She drinks 1/4 of a litre. How much orange juice does she have left? Write your answer as a decimal number.

atoms.a: Write the fraction in its simplest form.
Write the division as a decimal number to find out how much orange juice Olivia has left.
atoms.b: Olivia has <mat><gap>0.5</gap></mat> litres of orange juice left.

atoms.a: To get one half of a litre of orange juice, you need 4 oranges. How many oranges would you need to make one litre?
